words.definition: Fairly large in amount or degree.
words.example: The new policy led to a **substantial** drop in unemployment.

words.definition: As a result of something just mentioned.
words.example: It rained heavily all week; **consequently**, the festival was postponed.

words.definition: Mainly or mostly.
words.example: The workforce in this sector is **predominantly** made up of young graduates.

words.definition: Likely to cause disagreement between people.
words.example: Immigration remains a **contentious** issue in many countries.

words.definition: To make a problem or its effects less severe.
words.example: New building codes were introduced to **mitigate** earthquake damage.

words.definition: Reasonable or likely to be true.
words.example: She offered a **plausible** explanation for the delay.

words.definition: Complete and including everything necessary.
words.example: The report gives a **comprehensive** overview of the industry.

words.definition: Having more than one possible meaning; unclear.
words.example: The instructions were so **ambiguous** that nobody knew what to do.

words.definition: Existing as a hidden or less obvious cause of something.
words.example: Poverty is often an **underlying** cause of poor health.

words.definition: A connection between two things where one tends to change along with the other.
words.example: Researchers found a strong **correlation** between exercise and mental wellbeing.

words.definition: Possible to do easily or practically.
words.example: It isn't **feasible** to finish the project in just two days.

words.definition: Certain to happen and impossible to avoid.
words.example: As the city grew, traffic congestion became **inevitable**.

words.definition: To become, or to make, smaller or less important.
words.example: Public interest in the project began to **diminish** over time.

words.definition: To make an action or process easier.
words.example: The new software will **facilitate** communication between departments.

words.definition: Widespread or common in a particular place or at a particular time.
words.example: Obesity has become increasingly **prevalent** in developed countries.

words.definition: An idea or belief about something.
words.example: Many people reject the **notion** that money guarantees happiness.

words.definition: Happening after something else.
words.example: The **subsequent** meeting was cancelled due to low attendance.

words.definition: To form or be a part of something as a whole.
words.example: Women **constitute** nearly half of the university's student body.

words.definition: To obtain or receive something from a particular source.
words.example: Much of the country's income is **derived** from tourism.

words.definition: A possible effect or result of an action or decision.
words.example: The policy change has serious **implications** for small businesses.

words.definition: Having doubts about whether something is true or will work.
words.example: Many scientists remained **skeptical** of the new theory at first.

words.definition: Based on observation or experiment rather than theory alone.
words.example: The study relies on **empirical** evidence gathered over ten years.

words.definition: Logical and well organised; easy to follow.
words.example: Her essay presented a **coherent** argument from start to finish.

words.definition: To publicly support a particular cause or policy.
words.example: Many economists **advocate** for reduced trade barriers.

words.definition: A difference between things that should otherwise match.
words.example: There was a **discrepancy** between the two sets of figures.

words.definition: Able to continue over a long period without causing lasting damage.
words.example: The company adopted more **sustainable** farming methods.

words.definition: Very small in size, degree, or importance.
words.example: The new design offers only a **marginal** improvement in efficiency.

words.definition: To say that something is caused by a particular thing or person.
words.example: She **attributes** her success to years of hard work.

words.definition: A situation that seems to contradict itself but may still be true.
words.example: It's a strange **paradox** that richer countries often report lower happiness levels.

words.definition: Thorough, careful, and demanding of high standards.
words.example: The product went through **rigorous** testing before release.

words.definition: To gradually weaken something, often without it being obvious.
words.example: Corruption continues to **undermine** public trust in government.

words.definition: Able to adapt easily to many different functions or situations.
words.example: A **versatile** employee can move easily between different roles.

words.definition: Capable of working successfully; practical.
words.example: Solar power is now a **viable** alternative to fossil fuels in many regions.

words.definition: Strong and unlikely to fail or break down.
words.example: The economy showed **robust** growth despite global uncertainty.

words.definition: The cutting down of large areas of forest.
words.example: **Deforestation** in the region has accelerated over the past decade.

words.definition: A substance, especially a gas, released into the air.
words.example: Vehicle **emissions** are a major contributor to urban air pollution.

words.definition: Describing an energy source, like wind or sunlight, that is not used up.
words.example: The government aims to double **renewable** energy capacity by 2035.

words.definition: The variety of plant and animal life found in a particular habitat.
words.example: Coral reefs support an extraordinary level of marine **biodiversity**.

words.definition: A long period of unusually low rainfall.
words.example: The region has suffered its worst **drought** in fifty years.

words.definition: The process by which more people come to live in cities.
words.example: Rapid **urbanisation** has put enormous pressure on housing supply.

words.definition: The reduction in the amount of something over time.
words.example: The **depletion** of fish stocks has alarmed marine biologists.

words.definition: All the living things in an area, together with how they interact with their surroundings.
words.example: Removing one species can disrupt an entire **ecosystem**.

words.definition: A substance that causes harm to the environment.
words.example: Factories were ordered to reduce the **pollutants** released into the river.

words.definition: The protection of the natural environment and wildlife.
words.example: The organisation focuses on the **conservation** of endangered species.

words.definition: A situation in which there are too many people for the available resources.
words.example: Some experts blame food shortages partly on **overpopulation**.

words.definition: Systems for removing waste and dirty water to protect public health.
words.example: Poor **sanitation** remains a leading cause of disease in the region.

words.definition: A situation in which a place, especially a road, is overcrowded.
words.example: Traffic **congestion** costs the city millions in lost productivity each year.

words.definition: The basic physical systems a country needs, such as roads and power supplies.
words.example: The country needs to invest heavily in transport **infrastructure**.

words.definition: The forced movement of people away from their homes.
words.example: Flooding caused the **displacement** of thousands of families.

words.definition: An official rule that controls how something is done.
words.example: New **regulations** require factories to limit their emissions.

words.definition: The natural home or environment of a plant or animal.
words.example: Logging has destroyed much of the species' natural **habitat**.

words.definition: A town or city that has its own local government.
words.example: The **municipality** introduced a new recycling scheme last year.

words.definition: Money given by a government to reduce the cost of something.
words.example: Farmers receive a **subsidy** to grow certain crops.

words.definition: The use of goods, energy, or natural resources.
words.example: Household energy **consumption** rises sharply during winter.

words.definition: The process of something, especially land or the environment, being made worse.
words.example: Soil **degradation** threatens agricultural output in many regions.

words.definition: Unfair differences between groups of people in wealth, opportunity, or status.
words.example: Income **inequality** has widened in many developed economies.

words.definition: The general health, happiness, and safety of a person or group.
words.example: The reforms aim to improve the **welfare** of low-income families.

words.definition: Laws considered as a group, or the process of making laws.
words.example: New **legislation** was passed to protect coastal wetlands.

words.definition: To travel regularly between home and a place of work.
words.example: Many residents **commute** over an hour each way to the city centre.

words.definition: A site where large amounts of waste are buried in the ground.
words.example: Reducing packaging waste keeps more material out of **landfill**.

words.definition: The practice of farming, including growing crops and raising animals.
words.example: **Agriculture** remains the largest employer in several developing economies.

words.definition: The ability to recover quickly from difficulties or damage.
words.example: Coastal cities are investing in flood defences to improve **resilience**.

words.definition: A new plan or process introduced to achieve a particular goal.
words.example: The city launched an **initiative** to plant one million trees.

words.definition: The use of more resources than is necessary or sustainable.
words.example: Critics argue that **overconsumption** in wealthy nations drives much environmental damage.

words.definition: The process of making something impure by adding a harmful substance.
words.example: **Contamination** of the water supply forced the plant to shut down.

words.definition: A person's main way of earning enough money to live.
words.example: Fishing is the main **livelihood** for many coastal families.

words.definition: The quality of being easy to reach, enter, or use.
words.example: The new subway line greatly improved **accessibility** for disabled residents.

words.definition: To learn how to do something after some practice.
words.example: It took me a while to **get the hang of** driving on the left.

words.definition: To feel excited about something that is going to happen.
words.example: I really **look forward to** visiting my grandparents every summer.

words.definition: To decide on something.
words.example: I still haven't **made up my mind** about which course to take.

words.definition: Very busy, moving from one activity to another.
words.example: Between work and family, I'm constantly **on the go**.

words.definition: To spend time with someone you haven't seen in a while, sharing recent news.
words.example: We met for coffee to **catch up** after months apart.

words.definition: To have a friendly relationship with someone.
words.example: I **get along with** most of my colleagues really well.

words.definition: To start doing a new hobby or activity.
words.example: She decided to **take up** painting during the lockdown.

words.definition: To delay doing something.
words.example: I keep **putting off** cleaning out the garage.

words.definition: To find something by chance, or to give a particular impression.
words.example: He **comes across** as very confident in interviews.

words.definition: To happen in a particular way, especially one that was not expected.
words.example: The weather **turned out** much better than the forecast suggested.

words.definition: To manage to live or cope, especially with limited money or resources.
words.example: It's hard to **get by** on a part-time salary in this city.

words.definition: To raise a child, or to mention a topic in conversation.
words.example: She was **brought up** in a small village outside the capital.

words.definition: To understand or solve something after thinking about it.
words.example: It took me ages to **figure out** how the new app worked.

words.definition: To depend on someone or something.
words.example: Many rural communities **rely on** a single road for access to the city.

words.definition: To be noticeably better or different from others around it.
words.example: Her application really **stood out** among hundreds of others.

words.definition: To move or progress at the same rate as someone or something.
words.example: It's hard to **keep up with** how quickly technology changes.

words.definition: To start living a stable, quiet life, often after a period of travel or change.
words.example: After years abroad, they decided to **settle down** back home.

words.definition: To recover from something difficult, such as an illness or disappointment.
words.example: It took him months to **get over** the loss of his job.

words.definition: To investigate or examine something carefully.
words.example: The council agreed to **look into** residents' complaints about noise.

words.definition: To meet someone unexpectedly.
words.example: I **ran into** an old classmate at the airport last week.

words.definition: To save something, usually time or money, for a particular purpose.
words.example: I try to **set aside** a little money every month for savings.

words.definition: To resemble a parent or older relative in appearance or character.
words.example: She really **takes after** her mother in terms of ambition.

words.definition: For a feeling or effect to gradually disappear.
words.example: The excitement of the new job soon **wore off**.

words.definition: To say or do something that makes people feel more relaxed in a new or awkward situation.
words.example: The host told a joke to **break the ice** at the start of the meeting.

words.definition: To carefully consider the advantages and disadvantages of something.
words.example: We need to **weigh up** the pros and cons before deciding.

words.definition: To eventually find the time to do something.
words.example: I finally **got around to** fixing the leaking tap.

words.definition: To have just enough money to cover basic living costs.
words.example: With rising rent, it's getting harder to **make ends meet**.

words.definition: To relax and avoid stress or hard work.
words.example: After the exams, I just want to **take it easy** for a while.

words.definition: Feeling slightly unwell.
words.example: I'm feeling a bit **under the weather**, so I might skip the gym today.

words.definition: Happening suddenly and unexpectedly.
words.example: She called me **out of the blue** after years of silence.

words.definition: Having the same understanding or opinion as someone else about something.
words.example: Before we start the project, let's make sure we're **on the same page**.

words.definition: To say something directly, without unnecessary detail.
words.example: I'll **get straight to the point**: the project is behind schedule.

words.definition: Over a long period of time; eventually.
words.example: Buying quality tools costs more now but saves money **in the long run**.
